|alt_coat                    = National Coat of Arms

There are four types of '''elections in Pelaxia''': general elections, elections to the legislatures of the provinces (regional elections) and local elections. General elections and elections to the legislatures of the provinces are called after the mandate of the national or provincial legislature expires, usually five years after the last election, although early elections may occur. Elections to local councils (municipal and insular) are held on fixed dates but some local government bodies (including provincial councils) are not directly elected. For most elections party list PR is used for both the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate, but the plurality system is often used in local councils elections.

countries.title: Fhainnin_Popular_Republic
countries.snippet:
The Fhainnin Popular Republic was a constitutional monarchy which served as the de facto government of Faneria from the start of the [[Fhainnin Civil War]] until the formation of the [[Faneria|Republic of the Fhainn]] in 1917. It was the original provisional government of the Republican movement in Faneria, and prosecuted the war against the [[Council for the Preservation of the Throne]]. The FPR was constitutionally an elective republican government with a vestigial monarchy under Rih [[Glen Wynnys-Màrtainn]], but in practice operated as a military dictatorship under the leadership of [[Callac Cananach]] and the Nationalist-Republican Party.

countries.title: Telecommunications_in_Cartadania
countries.snippet:
{{Culture of Cartadania}}
'''Telecommunications in Cartadania''' are highly developed. It is served by an extensive system of automatic {{wp|telephone exchange}}s connected by modern networks of {{wp|fiber-optic}} cable, {{wp|coaxial cable}}, {{wp|microwave radio relay}}, and a domestic satellite system. The cellular telephone service is widely available, expanding rapidly to extremely rural areas, and includes roaming service to foreign countries, while those visiting countries where the operating carrier is also present continue service as usual. As a result of intensive capital expenditures, even some rural and remote areas have been rapidly modernized to the most advanced technology.

countries.title: Volinia
countries.snippet:
'''Volinia''', also called '''Nuyak''' in Volin, was a country in [[Crona]]. Volinia was founded by and is comprised of [[Indigeno-Calderan|Volins]], hence the exonym Volinia which means "Land of Volins". The name Volinia is relatively recent, and is used to describe specifically the time period in which the Volins were self-governing. This is in contrast with the endonym Nuyak, which refers to the island itself, and can also refer to modern day [[Calderan Republic|Caldera]].

countries.title: Fascist_Caldera
countries.snippet:
'''Fascist Caldera''' or '''Oligarch Caldera''', is the term for the political status of [[Calderan Republic|Caldera]] from 1600 until 2034. The term was first coined by former Volin Reform Party leader Den Fox in 1926, as he predicted a future where the [[Volkspartei]] would no longer be in control of the majority [[Indigeno-Calderan]] population. This period of time is characterized by absolute control of the country by the Volkspartei, where only a male person of Gothic origin could be elected as head of state. For most of the country's history, all politicians had to be male and Gothic as well.

{{MajorReconstruction}}

'''Postwar Varshan''' refers to the period of [[Varshan]]i history between the end of the [[Final War of the Deluge]] and the [[Dissolution of Varshan]] in [[2040]], encompassing both the [[League of Nations]] occupation of the country as well as its brief period of nominal independence under the Union of Varshan. During this time, Varshan underwent significant international reconstruction as well as dramatic internal changes in terms of culture, demography, and economics. The League occupation-era and Union-era are typically considered to represent the same period of time in Varshani history both because of continuing foreign influence but also because of continuing social transformation that occurred during that time.

countries.title: Nouvelle_Rousselle
countries.snippet: The '''Colony of Nowa Ruś''', later administered as '''Nouvelle Rousselle''', was a [[Slawišč league|Slawišč]] and subsequently [[Duchy of Marialanus|Marialanus]] possession on the northern [[Audonia|Audonian]] coast. Founded in 1505 as a defensive trading port and mineral extraction base, it became the most prosperous overseas territory of the Slawišč league until its conquest in 1599. Under Marialanus rule it shifted from a resource colony to a military hub, later evolving into a semi autonomous coastal territory before its destruction and annexation into the [[Jazéréan-Askari Khaganate]] in 1787. The colony lay on a subtropical humid coastline marked by flat terrain and a sheltered bay. The surrounding land lacked major rivers but offered a reliable anchorage and access to the foothills of a southern highland zone. parties.snippet:
This article discusses select [[Kiravian]] political parties that are neither represented in the [[Federal Stanora]], nor considered serious contenders for provincial legislative leadership or province-wide offices. These parties may have limited representation in provincial legislatures or be represented at the local (countyship and municipal) level only, while others hold no public offices at all. parties.snippet:
{{Urcea WIP}}

The '''Retainer Party''', '''Retainer Coalition''', or '''Pink Coalition''' refer to a semi-official alliance between the [[Union for National Solidarity (Urcea)|Union for National Solidarity]] and pro-[[Apostolic King of Urcea|monarchy]] members of the [[Social Labor Party (Urcea)|Social Labor Party]] in the [[Conshilía Daoni]]. The Coalition, established in September 2017, was formed in the wake of the vote scheduling the [[2018 Urcean institutional referendum]] on the future of the Monarchy.

The Retainer Party aims to be the primary pro-Monarchy campaign arm in the [[2018 Urcean institutional referendum]] as its primary purpose. It additionally functions as an organized bi-partisan opposition to the majority [[National Pact (Urcea)|National Pact]] elected in [[2015 Urcean Conshilía Daoni election|2015]], and seeks to preserve's [[Urcea]]'s welfare state and the present [[Constitution of Urcea]].

parties.snippet:
The '''Volkspartei''' (Gothic: People's Party) was the national political party of [[Fascist Caldera|Caldera]] from 1600 until 2034. They were the only political party allowed to run for Prime Leader, and because of this, the Volkspartei is considered to be one of the oldest active political parties in the world. The Volkspartei is controversial for only allowing people of Gothic descent into their membership, and for being the cause of several revolts and civil unrest in Caldera.

The [[Nasastan|National Federation of Nasastan]] is a federal parliamentary authoritarian republic characterized by a political system of [[Guided democracy|managed pluralism]]. Under the [[Constitution of Nasastan|Constitution of 1937]], political participation is structured through a unique asymmetric bicameral legislature that separates economic governance from sociocultural deliberation. While the country permits a degree of multiparty competition, the [[Ethnofederalist Social Nasastani National Party]] (SNNSP) functions as the dominant legal and administrative framework of the state. Political activity in Nasastan is divided according to the specific competencies of the two parliamentary chambers; The [[Purokal]] (Economic Chamber)''':''' Membership is strictly restricted to representatives of the SNNSP. Economic debate is not conducted between rival parties but within five internal ideological factions of the SNNSP, which range from far-left to far-right economic currents. ideologies.title: Pan-Cronanism
ideologies.snippet:
'''Pan-Cronanism''', a movement which has recently gained momentum in the 2020's, is the political ideology calling for the unification of states on the continent of [[Crona]] into a larger political entity, commonly in the form of supranational organizations, but also rarely in form of one of several unified Cronan superstates. The movement is most popular in southern Crona, with smaller movements elsewhere on the continent.

==Origins==
The Pan-Cronan movement emerged after the end of the [[Great Cronan War]] in the mid-late 1950s. It originally began as a movement of peace, intended to call for peaceful resolution to any further conflicts that could escalate into another Great War. As time went on, however, the movement grew into one that sought to join together the continent of Crona in some respect of unity and cooperation. Kronatan congressman [[Gregor Friedrich Mandel]] coined the term ''Pan-Cronanism'' in his 1961 speech to the [[Kronatan Legislature|Bundeskongress]], saying that "It is a necessary idea of brotherly cooperation between all the states of Crona to rebuild the relationships shaken by the war."

'''Shaftonist democracy''' (Coscivian: ''Śavtoplānoāritarisēn'', ''Śavtoþérmúāritarisēn'') is an ideology within the larger tradition of Shaftonist republicanism seeking to apply Shaftonic ideals and Shaftonist political theory in the context of modern {{wp|liberal democracy}}. 

Shaftonist democracy grew out of the modern Shaftonist political movement anchored in the [[Renaissance Party]] and underground networks of dissident intellectuals during Kirosocialism, and gained prominence amid the Mid-Kirosocialist period of political and socio-economic stagnation. It was posited as the vision of the [[Federalist Republican Alliance]] and the National Renewal Movement for a post-Kirosocialist future, and remains the main ideological line of the SRA caucus and most of its member-parties to this day.  

Shaftonist democracy can be characterised as an approach to politics that combines Shaftonist principles such as ''ixtévirsa'' ("higher order"), ''athnivirsa'' ("proper order"), ''uordhiria'' ("edification"), ''xarbonara'' ("continuity"), and ''valium'' ("duty"); with political structures and practices typical of [[Occidental]] liberal democracy. '''Restarkism''', ([[Cape Coscivian]]: ''Restarkizme'', archaically ''Rektarizm''), or '''the Four Principles''', is the founding ideology of the [[the Cape|Federacy of the Cape]]. Developed by [[Melvyn Kalma]], it is a philosophy with the aim of developing and uniting the Cape into a modern, [[Occidental]], and powerful state. As defined by him, it is a national liberation ideology with the broad goal of uniting the ethnically disparate peoples of the country and separating the new nation from its previous tribal and colonial roots. To this day, Restarkism remains the official constitutional {{wp|ideology|state ideology}} of the Federacy, and is the guiding philosophy of the {{wp|dominant-party system|dominant}} [[Republican Nationalist Party]]. 

Much of the ideology originated from various colonial reforms before the [[Cape War of Independence]], where the ideas of {{wp|civic nationalism}} and democracy took root. Following the independence of the Cape, Kalma took the earlier civic-nationalist and democratic ideals and combined them with the ideas of the budding {{wp|liberalism|liberal}} and {{wp|socialist}} movements of the Occident. ideologies.title: Pelaxian_Socialism
ideologies.snippet:
Pelaxian Socialism is a political, social, and economic philosophy of Marxist origing encompassing a range political theories, and social systems characterised by social ownership of the means of production. It includes the economic policies and movements associated with such systems. Social ownership can be public, collective, cooperative, or of equity. 

While no single definition encapsulates the many types of principles, social ownership is the one common element that has been higlighted in the 21st century. 

Historically Pelaxian Socialists disagreed about the degree to which social control or regulation of the economy is necessary, how far society should intervene and whether government, particularly existing government, is the correct vehicle for change. Pelaxian Socialism lines of thought have been divided in non-market and market forms. Non-market socialism substitutes factor markets and money with integrated economic planning and engineering or technical criteria based on calculation performed in-kind, thereby producing a different economic mechanism that functions according to different economic laws and dynamics than those of capitalism. A non-market socialist system eliminates the inefficiencies and crises traditionally associated with capital accumulation and the profit system in capitalism. The socialist calculation debate, originated by the economic calculation problem, concerns the feasibility and methods of resource allocation for a planned socialist system

ideologies.title: Urcean_socialist_philosophy
ideologies.snippet:
{{Urcea WIP}}

'''Urcean socialist philosophy''' is the study of the different strains of {{wp|socialist}} thought in [[Urcea]].
==Marxism==
Traditional readings of [[Carlos Marx]] have been popular in small circles in [[Urcea]] since the establishment of his works in the mid 19th century. Marx's discussion of the {{wp|Historical materialism|materialist reading of history}} described a system in which the feudal mode of production would give way to a capitalist mode followed by the creation of the socialist mode of production. Marx's view of the materialist progression, however, has caused divisions among Urcean Marxists since its inception; writing as a continental [[Sarpedon|Sarpedonian]], it was not clear to Marxists of the 19th century through today if this straight-forward model is applicable to Urcea. This fundamental disagreement led to the division of Marxists within Urcea between the "Traditionalist Marxists" and the "Particular Marxists".
===Traditionalist Marxists===
Traditionalist Marxists in [[Urcea]] argue that Urcean society is merely in the capitalist mode of production with a mix of particular institutions that provide a public benefit but do not otherwise change its historical state. The traditionalists point out that a {{wp|distributist}} economy is still, largely, a {{wp|market economy}} and that the means of production are still owned by private hands and serve the interests of private individuals. ideologies.title: Disurbanism
ideologies.snippet:
'''Disurbanism''' (Coscivian: ''Akasarisēn'', from ''aka-'' "away from" + ''sar'' "city, town") is an ideology and a design movement originating in [[Kiravia]] with relevance to urban and civil planning, politics, and culture. Disurbanism posits that the {{wp|city}} (and in many formulations, the {{wp|town}}) is a harmful and unnecessary formation and a poor way to organise human life, and that cities and towns as currently understood should be abandoned in favour of more geographically distributed patterns of settlement. Most disurbanists believe that while cities once served legitimate purposes, they have since been rendered obsolete by modern advances in communications and transportation technology, and that the utilitarian benefits of cities no longer justify the social, economic, and political costs of urbanocentrism.

Disurbanism can be distinguished from traditionalist-agrarian anti-urbanism in that disurbanists embrace technological modernity as enabling a mass escape from cities and support the diffusion of traditionally urban activities such as industry, commerce, and human services into the countryside, with the ultimate goal of erasing any clear distinction between agricultural rural areas and industrial/commercial urban ones. However, in practice there is significant overlap and coöperation between disurbanist and rural anti-urbanist currents.

ideologies.title: Commarcho_Capitalism
ideologies.snippet:
'''Commarcho Capitalism''' ([[Classical Latin|Latin]]: ''Capitalista Commarchismus''; [[Pelaxian language|Pelaxian]]: ''Comarcocapitalismo''; [[Brenadine Tainean|Reform Tainean]]: ''Comarkaukapitaulismau'') is one of the official ideologies of the {{wp|List of frivolous political parties|satirical political party}} the [[Party of National Acceleration]], a self-declared party of the "steelvetines" (''cabacerciopeladistas'') founded in 1998 by two {{wp|punk ideologies|punks}} in [[Las Joquis]], [[Castadilla]]. The name of the ideology comes from the ideologies of {{wp|communism}} and {{wp|anarcho-capitalism}}, making it a portmanteau of the two terms.

Followers of this ideology have often called it "the final evolutionary stage for the Castadillaan nation where everyone will be free to do as they please ten times over or more in the struggle against any and all forms of education". Political analysts often debate over whether commarcho capitalism is meant to be a jab at [[Velvetine Socialism|Velvetine socialism]], or a tongue-in-cheek attempt at presenting an "alternative" to the [[People's Democratic Party|PDP]], but each and every single one of them have reached a consensus that the ideology is designed to be an expression of the growing [[Rumapunk subculture|Castadillaan punk subculture]] much like the other satirical ideologies that have risen in the late 1990s.

ideologies.title: Puertegan_Path_to_Socialism
ideologies.snippet:
Puertegan Path to Socialism {{lang|es|(camino al socialismo de Puertego)}} is a {{wp|Marxist revisionist}} {{wp|socialist}} ideology based around a set of political theories and policies advocated for by the dominant party of Puertego the Puertegan White Flag communist Party that are seen by their proponents as representing {{wp|Marxism–Leninism}} but adapted and reformed to best serve Puertego for the modern circumstances it finds itself in. Most people consider the largest modern proponent of this ideology to be the current president of Puertego Matthias Torres, the primary principles advocated by him for the ideology are an opening of the formally state controlled economy to the rest of the world, a strong central government to help oversee this transition and to maintain public order during this transition, and the protecting of Puertegan culture and traditions in society.

== History ==
The name of the ideology was first coined by Erik Alférez the founder of the Puertegan White Flag Communist Party and first president of Puertego who called it "the only way I can see Puertego having a future on the world stage". Since that time however the ideology has branched out massively from Alférez's original vision which was focused largely on social and political reforms and only had minor plans for economic reforms to prevent the economy from collapsing however Alférez did not live long enough to enshrine this aspect of the ideology into law as he died from a stroke after only 3

ideologies.title: Velvetine_Socialism
ideologies.snippet:
'''Velvetine Socialism''' ([[Classical Latin|Latin]]: ''Socialismi Holoserica''; [[Pelaxian language|Pelaxian]]: ''Socialismo Velutíno''; [[Brenadine Tainean|Reform Tainean]]: ''Sausalism des Velaus''), also known as '''Castadillaan Socialism''', '''Democratic Revolutionary Socialism''', or '''Reformist Labourism''', is the form of socialist thought developed during the [[Velvet Revolution]] in [[Castadilla]] to realise a socialist revolution in a country ruled by a [[Estado Social (Castadilla)|nationalist dictatorship]] for decades through gradual {{wp|reformist}} means. It is the official ideology of the [[People's Democratic Party]]. Ostensibly a form of [[Livasism#Marxism-Livasism|Marxism-Livasism]], Velvetine Socialism is in practice a form of {{wp|market socialism}} with elements of {{wp|dirigism}} and {{wp|tripartism}}, though some political analysts have described the ideology as being more akin to {{wp|social democracy}} with lots of government intervention than any particular form of socialism. It consists of [[Livasism#Cabaceroism|Cabaceroism]], [[Livasism#Borbonism|Borbonism]], and [[Castadillaanism]] ([[Francisco Carvalho]]). Each of these theories are, according to the party constitution of the PDP, representative of the relevant policies utilised for a given time period.

ideologies.title: Nolanism
ideologies.snippet:
{{Stub}}

'''Nolanism''' is a strain of {{wp|liberalism|liberal}} thought within [[Urcea]] that advocates the complete adoption of liberal social and economic ideas while remaining neutral on political issues such as the structure of the [[Constitution of Urcea|constitution]] or [[Apostolic King of Urcea|monarchy]] for pragmatic reasons. Nolanists are generally regarded as a radical strain of {{wp|conservative liberalism|conservative liberals}}, with the ideology calling for no accomodation with ancient institutions in Urcea such as the [[Guilds (Urcea)|guild system]], the established [[Catholic Church]], and the prevalence of so-called vice laws. Nolanism is generally opposed to [[Crown Liberalism]] and views the emancipation of the individual and enshrinement of {{wp|civil rights}} at the center of Urcean society as its chief aims. Adherents of the ideology also denounce {{Wp|socialism}} and various left-wing movements, feeling that they often make the monarchy a politically distracting issue while making their civil rights-oriented goals more easily subject to {{wp|strawman}} dismissals. The ideology is named for Linar Orens-Nolan, a onetime [[National Pact (Urcea)|National Pact]] member of the [[Conshilía Daoni]] and mid-20th century thought leader.

The 2026 Pelaxian Defence White Paper is an official document published by the Pelaxian Ministry of Defence in the wake of the Akanatoa War. The document outline the MoD discoveries and challenges presented to the armed forces for the second half of of the 21st century as well as the actions needes to meet specific objectives.

== Introduction ==

The Pelaxian Ministry of Defence presents this Defence White Paper in conjunction with the DEFENSA 2050 strategy, aimed at addressing the identified shortcomings within the Pelaxian Armed Forces and enhancing our military capabilities to meet future challenges. This strategy outlines a comprehensive roadmap for modernization, acquisition, and development initiatives critical to ensuring the readiness and effectiveness of our armed forces.

== Challenges ==

The Pelaxian Armed Forces face several challenges, including the aging armored personnel carrier fleet, the absence of a modern Main Battle Tank, and the need for revitalization of the Marine Expeditionary Force. To address these challenges effectively, the DEFENSA 2050 strategy outlines strategic initiatives and priorities aimed at modernizing and enhancing our military capabilities across all branches. ideologies.title: Political_ideologies_in_Castadilla
ideologies.snippet:
Formal '''political ideologies in Castadilla''' are aligned based upon the {{wp|left-right political spectrum}}, an axis used to classify political positions in relation to their emphasis on either social equality or social hierarchy. Most [[Castadillaans]] identify as at least one of four main ideologies: {{wp|socialism}}, {{wp|liberalism}}, {{wp|conservatism}}, and {{wp|nationalism}}; it is very common for one to identify as being any combination of two of the four main ideologies, with {{wp|political polarization|political polarisation}} being largely miniscule for the most part thanks to the four ideological groups more or less cooperating with each other during the era of the provisional government after the end of the [[Velvet Revolution]].

[[Castadilla]], alongside [[Pelaxia]], have often been called the "cradle of socialism", and the main subsections within modern [[Socialism in Castadilla|Castadillaan socialism]] include [[Velvetine Socialism]], [[Livasism#Borbonism|Borbonism]], [[Livasism#Cabaceroism|Cabaceroism]], and even various flavours of socialist-aligned {{wp|social democracy}}; with Velvetine Socialism and Borbonism having emerged from the revolutionary left-wing factions of the Velvet Revolution while socialist-aligned social democracy developed throughout the latter half of the 19th Century and had gained prominence as the left-wing faction of the anti-Pascualist opposition groups which were formed in the late 1940s. ideologies.title: Kaidoism
ideologies.snippet:
[[File:Kaidoist flag.png|330px|thumb|Flag used by Kaidoists between 1840s and 1850s]]

'''Kaidoism''' ([[Pomorskitong]]: ''Kaidoézm'') is a [[Nasastan|Nasastani]] political ideology and movement based on the ideas of Načelnik [[Kréstofer Kaido]] (1800 - 1839). Emerging in the early 19th century, it represents one of the principal ideological offshoots of [[Resistanceism]], often described as Nasastan's own internally developed variant of socialist thought. Kaidoism emphasizes the pursuit of [[Final egalitarianism|final egalitarianism]], the gradual equalization and standardization of all facets of social and economic life under a state-managed order. Although initially associated with Kaido’s rule in the 1830s, the term Kaidoism did not enter common usage until the tenure of Načelnik [[Kats Kontor]] (1844 - 1849), whose public identification with Kaido's legacy led to its formal recognition as a distinct ideological tradition within Nasastani politics.

The term Kaidoism derives from the surname of Kréstofer Kaido, Načelnik of Nasastan between 1829 and 1839. The suffix -ism (''-ézm'' in Pomorskitong) was first applied during the late 1840s by political commentators under the [[Aristocratic Sovereignty of Nasastan]] to describe Kontor's attempts to restore elements of Kaido’s program.

Guided_democracy
ideologies.snippet:
'''Guided democracy''', also called '''directed democracy''' and '''managed democracy''', is a ''de jure'' {{wp|democracy|democratic}} {{wp|government|government}} that nonetheless functions as a ''de facto'' {{wp|Authoritarianism|authoritarian regime}} or, in some cases, as an outright {{wp|Autocracy|autocratic regime}}. Such forms of {{wp|Hybrid regime|hybrid regimes}} are legitimised by elections, but these elections do not serve to change the {{wp|State (polity)|state}}'s government in any meaningful way but rather are deemed as {{wp|sham election|shams}} designed to keep up the appearance of a {{wp|liberal democracy}}.

In a guided democratic system, elections are directly controlled and manipulated by the government; people are permitted to exercise their democratic rights, but the government ensures that voters cannot change public policy. While they ostensibly follow basic democratic principles, they generally are beholden to a variety of authoritarianism to keep democracy "on a leash". Under a managed democratic system, the state makes heavy use of {{wp|propaganda techniques}} to {{wp|Manufacturing Consent|manufacture consent}} from the governed, and at times might make extensive use of {{wp|electoral fraud}} techniques such as voter intimidation, disinformation, or even announcing a predetermined result without bothering to count the votes, to prevent the electorate from having any kind of impact on government policy.

ideologies.title: Kallistocracy
ideologies.snippet:
[[File:ZD kallistocracy Poster 1937.png|thumb|"Kallistocracy; Live for Another." Recruitment poster for the [[Zabitur'š z duzelzo|ZD Secret Service]], produced in late 1937 to encourage enlistment following the [[Paramilitary Revolution]] and prior to the adoption of the organization's revised insignia.]]
'''Kallistocracy''' ([[Pomorskitong]]: ''Kallistokracéa'', literally ''government for the best condition'') is a political and philosophical doctrine originating in [[Nasastan]] that holds that the primary purpose of the state is to preserve the most desirable form of ordinary human life for the majority of the population. Rather than defining the state through sovereignty, liberty, or divine authority, Kallistocracy argues that government exists to maximize collective convenience, social stability, and interpersonal trust while minimizing unnecessary struggle. The doctrine constitutes one of the central political expressions of [[Zmoric Philosophy]] and the [[Lakhe'žic]] principle of 'easy life', serving as the dominant ideological framework of the modern Nasastani state.

The term derives from the [[istroyan]] roots ''kallistos'' (''best'', ''most beautiful'', or ''ideal'') and ''kratos'' (''rule'' or ''government''), collectively interpreted in Nasastani political philosophy as "government for the best condition."
